subject: physical-education
successCriteria: The learner holds attempting the goal and evaluating the attempt carried through a safe attempt when available or a detailed simulation of the attempt, including a realistic setback and an honest evaluation afterwards, in whatever version their body and setting allow. Full transfer credit requires the goal, attempt plan, realistic setback, response, and evidence-based evaluation. A safe attempt or detailed simulation earns equal credit when it preserves every part of that challenge-and-revision evidence.
The learner names what degraded first and why, rather than reporting only whether it worked.
The learner compares this occasion with the earlier one and says what actually changed.
scoringGuidance: Score safe participation, skill cues, tactical reasoning, self-management, and revision. Accept any version of the task the learner’s body and setting allow as full credit when it supplies the stated transfer evidence. Never score body size, weight, body composition, appearance, speed alone, or comparison with another person. Full transfer credit requires the goal, attempt plan, realistic setback, response, and evidence-based evaluation. A safe attempt or detailed simulation earns equal credit when it preserves every part of that challenge-and-revision evidence.
masteryRule: Do not mark mastery from one session. Use safe participation, skill cues, tactical decisions, self-management, personal progress against the learner’s own stated task, and self-assessment — without body-size scoring; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions separated by time or setting.
remediation: Return to the simplest version of attempting the goal and evaluating the attempt — slower, smaller range, closer target, or seated — then rebuild.

adaptiveRoutes.action: Return to the simplest version of attempting the goal and evaluating the attempt — slower, smaller range, closer target, or seated — then rebuild.
Ask the learner to explain the cue or tactic behind attempting the goal and evaluating the attempt before adding intensity or complexity.
Confirm the specific cue that worked, offer one varied application of attempting the goal and evaluating the attempt, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable movement pattern neutrally, contrast it with the critical features, and schedule varied practice.

adaptiveRoutes.signal: pain, dizziness, breathlessness, or head impact
adaptiveRoutes.action: Stop immediately, tell an adult, and do not resume in this session. This is never recorded as a failed attempt.

Offer the adapted, seated, solo, or described version of attempting the goal and evaluating the attempt; the alternate route is full credit when it supplies the stated transfer evidence and is not logged as a refusal. Full transfer credit requires the goal, attempt plan, realistic setback, response, and evidence-based evaluation. A safe attempt or detailed simulation earns equal credit when it preserves every part of that challenge-and-revision evidence.

adaptiveRoutes.signal: transfer condition is too much today
adaptiveRoutes.action: Drop back to the first-pass version of attempting the goal and evaluating the attempt for this session and re-attempt the added demand on a later occasion. Reducing the demand is the correct response and is scored as full participation, but it does not itself satisfy the transfer evidence requirement.
Require accurate independent performance or description plus explanation on a later occasion or in a different setting before marking attempting the goal and evaluating the attempt mastered.

guardianOrParentVisibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose body data, fitness scores, photographs, video, recordings, or comparisons with other learners. For safety-critical units, record only the guardian confirmation that was required.

guardianSafetyReview.environment: Guardian approves the location and conditions.
guardianSafetyReview.movement_hazards: The challenge is the highest-demand task in the course. Guardian reviews and approves the goal, the preparation, and the attempt conditions before the attempt.
guardianSafetyReview.supervision_note: Guardian sets supervision for the attempt and may require it to be supervised or declined.

safetyAndPrivacyNotes: Use respectful, non-shaming language about bodies, ability, and effort.
Allow a pause, rest, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Check space, footwear, surface, weather, and equipment before movement.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing difficulty, head impact, or unsafe conditions and tell an adult.
Score skill, strategy, self-management, consistency, and reflection — never body size, weight, weight change, body composition, appearance, or comparison with another person.
Do not require weight, BMI, body-fat, body measurement, fitness-test norms, percentile ranks, calorie counts, or diet goals at any point.
Do not require a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as evidence; described, written, and demonstrated-to-one-adult evidence is the intended route.
Do not require performance in front of an audience, a group, or spectators.
The challenge is never a body-composition, weight, or appearance goal, is never compared to another person’s result, and is never required to be witnessed, filmed, or published.
